title: HP-MDR: High-performance and Portable Data Refactoring and Progressive Retrieval with Advanced GPUs
problem: Scientific data management lacks GPU-accelerated progressive compression; existing methods are CPU-based and leave GPU performance potential untapped for heterogeneous systems
method: HP-MDR optimizes bitplane and lossless encoding on GPUs; incorporates pipeline optimization with progressive retrieval; enables QoI-driven error-controlled retrieval

title: A 50Gb/s Burst-Mode NRZ Receiver with 5-Tap FFE, 7-Tap DFE and 15ns Lock Time in 28nm CMOS for Symmetric 50G-PON
problem: 50G PON receivers face severe inter-symbol interference (ISI) from chromatic dispersion and limited photonic bandwidth; burst-mode operation requires rapid lock (<15ns) with high SNR tolerance. Existing designs trade fast lock for equalization depth (1-tap DFE insufficient for 50G).
method: A burst-mode receiver in 28nm CMOS integrates 5-tap FFE (3 pre, 1 post) and 7-tap DFE (4 floating post-cursors up to 16th tap) for deep ISI cancellation. Edge equalization with fast-lock circuitry achieves 15ns lock time while APD integration supports standard-defined high-gain photodiode operation.

title: Exo 2: Growing a Scheduling Language
problem: User-schedulable languages (USLs) fix a single design point for what programmers control and what is automated, but no universal control/automation split exists even in narrow domains, causing USLs to be inextensible when new hardware targets or optimization strategies emerge.
method: Exo 2 enables users to define new scheduling operations externally to the compiler by composing a set of trusted fine-grained primitives (actions for modifying code, inspection for querying code structure, and references for pointing to code locations). The key mechanism is Cursors, a new abstraction that unifies code references across actions, inspections, and scheduling library composition, allowing safe user-defined scheduling transformations. Users build scheduling libraries that amortize transformation effort across related kernels without modifying the compiler internals.

title: PipeLink: A Pipelined Resource Sharing System for Dataflow High-Level Synthesis
problem: Dynamically scheduled HLS produces pipelined dataflow circuits, but coordinating pipelined function calls and shared resources is difficult without centralized control, limiting support for general software programs.
method: PipeLink decomposes synthesis into compilation and linking stages, enabling fully-pipelined access to shared functions in asynchronous dataflow circuits. Uses asynchronous design principles for both pipelined function units and pipelined memory access in a unified framework.

title: Scaling Laws of Graph Neural Networks for Atomistic Materials Modeling
problem: GNNs for atomistic materials modeling remain small (millions of parameters) compared to LLMs (billions); lack of scaling guidance limits accuracy and applicability to complex materials discovery tasks.
method: Develops foundational GNN with billions of parameters trained on terabyte-scale datasets; incorporates LLM-inspired training techniques (efficient data/model management) to enable large-scale GNN training and deployment; explores three scaling dimensions: architecture, dataset size, and training method applicability.

title: Bridging the Gap between Unstructured SpMM and Structured Sparse Tensor Cores
problem: Sparse-dense Matrix Multiplication (SpMM) on Tensor Cores is inefficient for unstructured sparse matrices due to low block-wise density, causing computational waste. Specialized Sparse Tensor Cores (SpTCs) require strict 2:4 or 1:2 structured sparsity, creating a mismatch with real-world unstructured sparse data.
method: MP-SpMM: A Matching and Padding approach inspired by graph theory's maximum matching problem to transform unstructured sparse matrices into structured sparsity patterns compatible with SpTCs. Includes novel storage format and highly optimized GPU kernel.

title: On the Compressibility of Floating-Point Data in Posit and IEEE-754 Representation
problem: The compressibility of posit floating-point format versus IEEE 754 is unknown, limiting understanding of posit's practical benefits for storage-intensive HPC applications.
method: Comparative evaluation of 5 general-purpose lossless compressors (bzip2, XZ, etc.) and new algorithms synthesized via LC framework. 14 single-precision datasets from SDR-Bench suite encoded in both float and posit format. Analysis of compression ratios and compressor performance.

title: Connected-Component Labeling Using HLS for High-Energy Particle Physics Instruments
problem: High-level synthesis (HLS) can reduce FPGA development time, but effectiveness for complex signal processing kernels (like island detection) is unclear.
method: HLS implementation of island detection with 1D/2D configurations and 4-way/8-way connected-component labeling; report resource usage, throughput, and required optimizations.

title: 21.5 A Fully Integrated Multi-Phase Voltage Regulator with Enhanced Light-Load-Efficiency Peak of 86%, Featuring an Autonomous Mode Transition from Hard-Switching to Soft-Switching to Discontinuous Conduction Mode in 3nm FinFET CMOS
problem: Fully integrated voltage regulators (FIVRs) face efficiency challenges across the power spectrum: high efficiency at peak power (current surges) but poor efficiency at idle loads; soft-switching and DCM modes reduce ripple but degrade efficiency under high load.
method: 3nm FIVR with autonomous mode transition from hard-switching (high load) to soft-switching to discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) at light load, maintaining droop response while achieving 86% peak light-load efficiency.

title: BiNeuroRAM: Energy-Efficient ReRAM-Based PIM for Accurate Bipolar Spiking Neural Network Acceleration
problem: Existing ReRAM-based neuromorphic accelerators suffer from high sensing power and accuracy degradation when running spiking neural networks, limiting their deployment.
method: BiNeuroRAM uses ReRAM-based processing-in-memory with three innovations: (1) support for spike-tracing bipolar-integrate-and-fire (ST-BIF) neurons enabling higher accuracy; (2) low-power voltage sense amplifier (LPVSA) reducing ReRAM read power by 14.7-58.2x via optimized sensing; (3) asynchronous micro-architecture exploiting event-driven SNN sparsity to maximize throughput.

title: Intel IPU E2200: Second Generation Infrastructure Processing Unit (IPU)
problem: Data center infrastructure requires specialized processing for networking, security, and telemetry offloads; Intel IPU E2200 targets accelerating infrastructure workloads beyond GPU/CPU capability.
method: IPU E2200 integrates a multi-core compute fabric optimized for packet processing and infrastructure workloads, with hardware accelerators for cryptography and telemetry collection, connected via high-speed fabric to enable efficient offloading from general-purpose compute.

title: SYLQ-SV: Scaling Symbolic Execution of Hardware Designs with Query Caching
problem: Symbolic execution of hardware designs (in SystemVerilog) suffers from path explosion, making full security and functional verification intractably expensive. Existing engines lack comprehensive SystemVerilog language support and do not exploit redundancy across SMT queries generated during path exploration.
method: SylQ-SV is a dedicated SystemVerilog symbolic execution engine that caches SMT queries across paths. When the engine encounters a query that is semantically equivalent to a previously solved one, it retrieves the cached result rather than re-invoking the SMT solver, avoiding redundant computation. The engine also provides full SystemVerilog language coverage including SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) to support end-to-end verification of open-source designs.

title: AI Revolution Driven by Memory Technology Innovation
problem: The 'memory wall' phenomenon—the growing mismatch between compute speed and memory bandwidth—is intensifying in the AI era. Conventional memory architectures cannot support the bandwidth, latency, and capacity demands of modern AI algorithms, limiting system performance and algorithm innovation.
method: The abstract outlines that memory companies have been developing multiple solutions over several years to address power, performance, and capacity requirements for AI systems. These technologies are being gradually integrated into products to bridge the memory-compute gap.

title: Guiding Application Users via Estimation of Computational Resources for Massively Parallel Chemistry Computations
problem: Users struggle to predict resource requirements (nodes, tile sizes, runtime) for expensive chemistry computations on supercomputers, leading to suboptimal submissions and wasted allocations.
method: Machine learning models (Gradient Boosting, Active Learning) to predict CCSD execution time for given problem sizes and parameter values, enabling resource optimization on Frontier and Aurora.

title: KernelGPT: Enhanced Kernel Fuzzing via Large Language Models
problem: Kernel fuzzing effectiveness depends critically on syscall specifications that define the syntax and semantics of system calls, but generating these specifications is largely manual work, leaving large numbers of important syscalls uncovered and limiting automated kernel vulnerability discovery.
method: KernelGPT uses large language models to automatically generate and repair syscall specifications for kernel fuzzing. The system prompts an LLM with kernel source code and documentation to synthesize syscall specifications in the format expected by the Syzkaller fuzzer, then uses an iterative refinement loop where fuzzing feedback is fed back to the LLM to repair invalid or incomplete specifications. This LLM-guided specification generation covers previously uncovered syscalls and improves the semantic validity of generated syscall sequences.

title: HyCMAx: Power-Efficient Hybrid CMOS-Memristor Based Approximate Dividers for Error-Resilient Applications
problem: Approximate computing traditionally uses CMOS technology; exploring hybrid CMOS-memristor approaches can yield further performance and power gains.
method: Hybrid CMOS-memristor approach for approximate circuit design. Proposes approximate subtractor then uses it to implement restoring divider in hybrid CMOS-memristor topology at 28nm CMOS node.
